title: NFLX: small two-step long in a de-rated cash compounder at ~18x 2027 EPS; the Oct 20 print and the January 2027 guide settle the engagement debate
call_reason: The published 12-month target of $75.49 is 8.5% above the $69.58 close and the research target (12m) of $80.00 is 15.0% above it, at medium conviction; size is capped by the supervisor at ~8% because the engagement debate is unresolved and earnings are three weeks out.
one_liner: Netflix has de-rated to ~18x 2027 consensus EPS on an engagement scare that has not yet reached churn (2% vs a 4% industry average) or pricing, while recurring FCF of ~$11.3-11.7B and a ~3-4% annual share shrink keep compounding per-share value. We buy 11 shares in two tranches around the Oct 20 print, target $75.49 / research target (12m) $80, take profit $97.77, stop at the $51 thesis break.

thesis.point: 1. Per-share cash compounding is intact and is being bought back cheaply.
thesis.evidence: Recurring 2026 FCF is ~$11.3-11.7B (the $11B pre-fee guide incl. the ~$700M Brazil deposit, vs $12.5B including the after-tax WBD fee), implying ~$13.0-13.5B in 2027. Net debt is only $5.24B (A2/A), and Q2 buybacks retired 52.9M shares, shrinking the 4.164B count ~3-4% a year.

thesis.point: 2. Monetisation shows no damage from the engagement debate yet.
thesis.evidence: Antenna July churn is 2% vs a 4% average for major services; the 2026 upfront nearly doubled ad commitments and the ad tier passed 250M monthly active viewers, with ads ~$3B in 2026. The fall season (~40% of annual gross adds) is the next test.

thesis.point: 3. The multiple already discounts a lot; the bar for the print is low.
thesis.evidence: At $69.58 the stock trades ~18x 2027 consensus EPS of $3.82 with 2028 at $4.56, near Wells Fargo's 15x bear multiple ($57 PT) after Wells Fargo and HSBC downgrades in September. Our research target (12m) of $80 needs only ~19x NTM EPS of ~$4.25 and a 4.5% FCF yield, not a return to the old 30x+.

variant_view: We sit between the two consensus views. The options market's distribution (result.json market_only) is centred at $70.19 with P(gain) 0.51, i.e. it prices no edge; we have $75.49 and P(gain) 0.58 because the forecasters see churn, ad growth and buybacks absorbing the engagement drag. The sell-side is far more bullish (weighted median PT $95, Deutsche Bank upgrade to Buy at $95 on 9/29, Wells Fargo $57 underweight); we stay well below it because peer de-ratings of quality large caps (DIS, PYPL, NKE, ADBE) have a median ~-6% follow-through over the next 12 months, so we do not underwrite a re-rating before the January 2027 guide. The real variant view is modest: the market is treating an engagement metric (Nielsen 7.8% share vs YouTube 14.2%; Wells Fargo ~-4% y/y hours per member in H2'26) as if it were already a revenue problem.

valuation.methods: Supervisor research target (12m) $80 (five forecasters $77-83, mean $80.3) = 60/40 blend of (a) P/E: NTM EPS at Sep-2027 of 0.25x$3.82 + 0.75x$4.56 = $4.38, less ~3% engagement haircut = $4.25, at 19x = ~$81; and (b) FCF: NTM FCF ~$14.5B at a 4.5% yield, less $5.24B net debt, over ~4.08B diluted shares = ~$77.7. The published 12-month target ($75.49, the median of the blended market/forecaster distribution) sits below the research target (12m) because the options market centres near spot; take profit $97.77 is the 75th percentile, stop $51 is the thesis break (~13.4x 2027 EPS, ~6.6% FCF yield).

catalysts.event: Paramount Skydance closes its WBD acquisition (all regulatory conditions met in Aug; 12-state AG settlement Sep 21)
catalysts.why_it_moves: Creates a combined HBO Max/Paramount+ rival with ~$80B of debt; integration plans and bundling/pricing signal how hard it will compete for subscribers and content.
catalysts.watch: Streaming bundle/pricing announcements, content-spend guidance and leverage of the combined company.

catalysts.event: First Nielsen Gauge on the recalibrated methodology (ARF DASH universe), covering the start of the fall TV season
catalysts.why_it_moves: Nielsen share (7.8% vs YouTube 14.2% in July) is the core of the bear case; a further drop under the new method would be read as confirmation even though it is a methodology break.
catalysts.watch: Netflix share of TV time vs the July 7.8% and YouTube's lead; any restatement of history under the new method.

catalysts.event: Q3 2026 results and Q4 guide (letter 1:01pm PT, video interview 1:45pm PT)
catalysts.why_it_moves: First print since the September downgrades; the Q4 guide and any 2027 framing set the growth path the multiple hangs on. Q2's slight beat with a lower outlook sent the stock down after hours.
catalysts.watch: Revenue vs $12.86B guide, 33.2% operating margin, EPS $0.82; Q4 guide vs the $51.2B / 31.5% FY26 plan; engagement and ad-revenue commentary; Q3 buyback pace and FCF vs the ~$12.5B FY guide; early 2027 growth/margin framing (~10% growth, 33-34% margin needed).

catalysts.event: Antenna churn and sign-up reads through the fall acquisition season
catalysts.why_it_moves: Churn at 2% is the evidence that engagement loss has not reached monetisation; Sep-Dec is ~40% of annual gross adds, so a rise here would validate the bear case.
catalysts.watch: Netflix monthly churn above ~2.5%; gross adds vs prior years; ad-tier mix.

catalysts.event: NFL Thanksgiving Eve game on Netflix (Packers at Rams), first of its kind
catalysts.why_it_moves: Live-sports tentpoles drive sign-ups and ad inventory and counter the engagement narrative; a streaming failure would hurt.
catalysts.watch: Reported viewership, stream stability, ad sell-out.

catalysts.event: Fury vs. Joshua heavyweight fight streamed live on Netflix (reported by trade/fan press, not yet verified in a company release)
catalysts.why_it_moves: A global live event at no extra cost; another engagement and sign-up spike for Q4.
catalysts.watch: Concurrent viewers; Q4 net-add commentary in January.

catalysts.event: NFL Christmas Day doubleheader exclusively on Netflix
catalysts.why_it_moves: Highest-profile ad inventory of the year; supports the ad-scaling leg of the thesis.
catalysts.watch: Viewership vs 2025 Christmas games; advertiser demand.

catalysts.event: Q4 2026 results and first full-year 2027 revenue, margin and FCF guidance
catalysts.why_it_moves: The main re-rating or de-rating event: ~10% 2027 growth with 33-34% margin supports the $80 research target (12m); high-single-digit growth or a flat margin is the bear path toward the $51 thesis break.
catalysts.watch: 2027 revenue growth vs ~10%, operating margin vs 33-34%, 2027 FCF vs ~$13.0-13.5B, buyback size, ad-revenue target.

catalysts.why_it_moves: Direct test of Wells Fargo's ~-4% y/y hours-per-member call for H2'26.
catalysts.watch: Total hours and hours per member y/y; share of views from top titles.

risks.risk: Engagement erosion reaches churn and pricing power (YouTube and creators taking TV time).
risks.signpost: Antenna churn above ~2.5% for two consecutive months, Netflix share falling further on the recalibrated Gauge, or a weaker take-rate on the next price increase.

risks.risk: The January 2027 guide shows high-single-digit growth and a stalled margin, cutting 2027/28 EPS.
risks.signpost: A Q4 guide on Oct 20 below the implied $51.2B FY26 plan, or 2027 framing under ~10% growth / ~33% margin.

risks.risk: The de-rating persists even if fundamentals hold (peer base rate: median ~-6% follow-through in 12 months).
risks.signpost: Stock fails to rally on a clean Oct 20 print and stays below ~$63 into January.

risks.risk: A large debt-funded acquisition (Lionsgate interest was reported and denied in June) diverts buyback capacity.
risks.signpost: Formal offer reports, new bond issuance beyond refinancing, or a slower Q3/Q4 buyback pace.

trade.position: 11 sh (~$765, 7.65% of the $10,000 book; capped by the supervisor's 8% limit; ~$204 loss at the stop)
trade.entry: Two tranches per the supervisor: ~half (5-6 sh) now near $69.58, the rest after the Oct 20 Q3 print and Q4 guide (by early November) if the guide holds. Decider ladder: add toward 13 sh below ~$63.32, trim toward 9 sh above ~$70.28 while the target-weighted sizing stays in force.
trade.exit_or_add: Exit on a close below $51 (thesis break) or on a January 2027 guide for high-single-digit growth with a flat margin. Add on weakness below ~$63 without a fundamental break, or after a January guide of ~10% growth and 33-34% margin with churn still ~2%. Take profit at $97.77.

what_changes_our_mind: Antenna churn rising above ~2.5% through the fall season, or the H2'26 engagement report showing hours per member falling faster than -4% y/y alongside slowing ad growth.
A Q4 guide on Oct 20 or a January 2027 guide pointing to <10% 2027 revenue growth or margin below ~33%, which would cut EPS rather than just the multiple.
On the upside: a January guide of ~10%+ growth with a 34%+ margin and a stable share on the recalibrated Nielsen Gauge would justify adding toward the research target (12m) of $80.
